past_medical_history: Frontotemporal dementia (behavioral variant bvFTD) — diagnosed 16 months ago at academic medical center
family_history: Father had severe personality change in late 60s — possibly FTD, never formally diagnosed

social_history.living_situation: Lives with husband; recently hired full-time caregiver due to behavioral disinhibition

patient.chief_complaint: Rapid deterioration with new gait impairment and urinary incontinence in patient with known bvFTD — neurology requesting second opinion
patient.history_present_illness: A 73-year-old retired judge with a prior diagnosis of behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD, diagnosed 16 months ago) was referred for a second opinion after her caring neurologist noted a new and accelerating pattern of decline that included gait impairment and urinary incontinence — features atypical for typical bvFTD trajectory. At the time of initial bvFTD diagnosis, she had a 2-year history of personality change (disinhibition, inappropriate social behavior, loss of empathy), executive dysfunction, and mild memory impairment. MRI at that time showed frontal lobe atrophy and the clinical diagnosis of bvFTD was made. She was started on sertraline with modest behavioral benefit. Over the past eight months, however, she has developed new features: (1) progressive shuffling wide-based gait that was not present at bvFTD diagnosis; (2) urinary incontinence — three accidents per week requiring protective pads; (3) accelerated cognitive decline beyond expected bvFTD trajectory. Her husband reports that her gait deterioration is the most alarming new feature — she now requires a walker and has had four falls. He notes her walking looks 'frozen' compared to her FTD trajectory. A repeat MRI obtained six months ago showed enlarged ventricles with Evans index 0.35 — not present on the 16-month prior MRI (Evans 0.27 at that time). The primary consulting neurologist requests evaluation for superimposed NPH on bvFTD versus revised diagnosis. The critical question is whether this represents NPH (treatable) superimposed on bvFTD, or atypical bvFTD progression, or NPH with bvFTD-like behavioral features (behavioral NPH).

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert but behaviorally disinhibited — made an inappropriate comment to the nurse. Oriented to person and approximate date. MoCA 17/30. Severe executive dysfunction. Minimal insight. Perseverative speech. Anomia mild.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Normal. No papilledema. Upward gaze mildly slow — possible PSP feature noted.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal tone and strength. No rigidity. No tremor.
neurological_exam.gait: Wide-based, markedly magnetic shuffling gait with bilateral freezing. Very short steps. TUG 38 seconds. 10-meter walk 30 seconds. Cannot tandem walk. Pull test — multiple steps backward.
neurological_exam.additional: Behavioral disinhibition evident (tactile/grasp behavior). Frontal lobe release signs prominent: bilateral grasp reflexes, snout, palmomental. No nuchal rigidity.

signal_characteristics.description: Partial DESH — confounded by frontal atrophy
Mildly reduced midbrain volume — hummingbird sign equivocal

mri.impression: Complex picture: (1) Interval ventriculomegaly (Evans 0.27→0.35) superimposed on bvFTD-pattern frontal atrophy. (2) Callosal angle 80° meets NPH criterion. (3) Equivocal DESH given frontal atrophy. (4) Mild midbrain volume reduction raises PSP as possibility. The differential remains: (A) NPH superimposed on bvFTD, (B) behavioral NPH (NPH mimicking bvFTD), (C) PSP with NPH-range ventriculomegaly. CSF biomarkers, FDG-PET, and tap trial are essential for further characterization. Clinical correlation recommended.

special_tests.phospho_tau: 24 pg/mL (normal — not consistent with AD tau)
special_tests.neurofilament_light_NfL: 2840 pg/mL — markedly elevated (consistent with aggressive neurodegeneration, FTD-spectrum)

csf.interpretation: Opening pressure: 17 cmH2O. WBC: 2 cells/mcL (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 46 mg/dL. Glucose: 68 mg/dL (ratio 0.74). cytology: No malignant cells. beta_amyloid_42: 684 pg/mL (normal — no AD amyloid pathology). total_tau: 384 pg/mL (elevated — consistent with FTD-spectrum neurodegeneration). phospho_tau: 24 pg/mL (normal — not consistent with AD tau). neurofilament_light_NfL: 2840 pg/mL — markedly elevated (consistent with aggressive neurodegeneration, FTD-spectrum).

specialized_test.test_type: High-volume tap trial (38 mL) with gait analysis
specialized_test.impression: Borderline-negative single tap trial: 18% TUG improvement — just below the 20% threshold. Cognitive and behavioral improvement minimal. This is consistent with limited NPH component in the context of dominant bvFTD/FTD-spectrum neurodegeneration. Extended lumbar drainage is recommended. However, the markedly elevated NfL suggests aggressive neurodegeneration that may limit shunt response.
recommended_actions: Extended lumbar drainage trial before excluding NPH component
FDG-PET to map metabolic pattern (frontal/temporal vs parietal — distinguishes bvFTD from NPH-dominant)
PSP evaluation — video oculomotor exam, consider MRI midbrain volumetry

findings.result: Bilateral frontal and anterior temporal hypometabolism — FTD-pattern (bvFTD). Additional frontal hypometabolism out of proportion to atrophy, consistent with hydrocephalus-related frontal dysfunction.

quantitative_data.pattern: Bifrontal-anterior temporal hypometabolism — bvFTD pattern dominant

output.impression: FDG-PET pattern is consistent with bvFTD (bifrontal-anterior temporal hypometabolism). Additional frontal hypometabolism may reflect NPH component. No posterior parietal hypometabolism (AD excluded). No midbrain hypometabolism typical of PSP. Pattern supports bvFTD as primary diagnosis with NPH as treatable superimposed condition.
recommended_actions: Tap trial extended drainage to further assess NPH contribution

findings.behavioral: Caregiver notes slight reduction in behavioral outbursts at 72h

output.impression: Extended drainage reveals meaningful NPH component: 32% TUG improvement at 72h. Single tap was false-negative. However, behavioral symptoms show only modest improvement — consistent with bvFTD as dominant neurological substrate for behavior. VP shunt is reasonable for gait and urinary improvement. Cognitive and behavioral benefit will be limited by bvFTD.
recommended_actions: VP shunt with appropriate counseling on limited behavioral/cognitive benefit
Goals: gait improvement and fall reduction, not behavioral normalization

output.test_type: Video oculomotor examination and midbrain volumetry

findings.finding: Mild slowing of vertical saccades — velocity slightly below normal but not diagnostic of PSP
Midbrain-pons area ratio 0.54 (borderline — PSP threshold 0.52 on this scanner)
No square wave jerks. No complete vertical gaze palsy.

output.impression: Borderline PSP features — mildly slow vertical saccades, borderline midbrain-pons ratio. Full PSP criteria not met (no complete vertical gaze palsy, no prominent axial rigidity, no falls from postural instability alone before this stage). PSP possible but not confirmed. Given FDG-PET frontal pattern and NPH response to drainage, bvFTD-NPH copathology is more likely than PSP.

output.query: frontotemporal dementia genetic testing C9orf72 GRN MAPT family history NPH overlap

results.title: Genetic FTD — C9orf72, GRN, MAPT and clinical phenotypes
results.key_finding: C9orf72 FTD can present with mixed phenotypes including ventriculomegaly; GRN mutations produce TDP-43 pathology; genetic testing is clinically relevant in bvFTD with positive family history

results.title: NPH mimicking bvFTD — case series
results.key_finding: NPH can produce behavioral disinhibition and executive dysfunction mimicking bvFTD in ~15% of cases; NfL and CSF tau help distinguish

output.summary: Given positive family history (father — possible FTD), genetic testing for C9orf72, GRN, and MAPT mutations is clinically indicated. If genetic FTD confirmed, prognosis for shunting is reduced but gait improvement remains a realistic goal. The elevated NfL (2840 pg/mL) suggests active FTD neurodegeneration beyond NPH alone.

output.impression: Negative amyloid PET. Excludes Alzheimer's disease copathology. Confirms TDP-43 or tau FTD-spectrum pathology as the neurodegenerative substrate (consistent with CSF normal p-tau). NPH-bvFTD dual diagnosis confirmed.

output.query: VP shunt bvFTD NPH copathology goals of care prognosis

results.title: VP shunt in patients with concurrent FTD and NPH — outcomes and ethics
results.key_finding: VP shunt in NPH-FTD copathology improves gait and reduces falls in majority; behavioral and cognitive improvement very limited; decision requires discussion of bvFTD prognosis and caregiver capacity for post-shunt care

output.summary: VP shunt is reasonable with proper goal-setting. Realistic expectations: gait improvement and fall reduction (primary goals); behavioral and cognitive improvement very limited by bvFTD. Husband and caregiver capacity for post-shunt monitoring is essential. Overall prognosis is poor due to progressive bvFTD, but improving gait reduces immediate fall risk and caregiver burden.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: NPH superimposed on behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (NPH-bvFTD copathology)

differential.key_features: Interval ventriculomegaly, extended drainage response (32%), callosal angle 80° confirm NPH component. bvFTD is present but NPH is superimposed and treatable.
Mildly slow vertical saccades, borderline MPAR. Full PSP criteria not met. FDG-PET pattern more consistent with bvFTD than PSP.

differential.diagnosis: Behavioral NPH mimicking bvFTD (without true FTD)
differential.key_features: NfL 2840 pg/mL markedly elevated — indicates substantial neurodegeneration beyond NPH. FDG-PET frontal pattern. bvFTD is a real concurrent diagnosis, not an artifact of NPH behavior.
Normal amyloid-42 (684 pg/mL), negative amyloid PET (CL 14), normal p-tau. AD excluded.

optimal_actions.action: Brain MRI comparing to prior — ventriculomegaly evolution
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Interval ventriculomegaly (Evans 0.27→0.35), callosal angle 80°, frontal atrophy from bvFTD, equivocal DESH

optimal_actions.action: CSF biomarkers including NfL and FTD markers
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Normal amyloid (no AD), elevated total tau/NfL (FTD neurodegeneration), normal p-tau; normal OP; 18% single-tap TUG improvement

optimal_actions.action: Extended lumbar drainage (72h) — single tap negative; confirm NPH
optimal_actions.expected_finding: 32% TUG improvement at 72h — confirms NPH component

optimal_actions.action: Goals-of-care discussion and VP shunt with appropriate expectations
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Shunt for gait/fall reduction; behavioral/cognitive improvement limited by bvFTD

critical_actions: Obtain CSF NfL and FTD biomarkers — markedly elevated NfL distinguishes FTD from NPH alone
FDG-PET is essential to map metabolic pattern and distinguish bvFTD from behavioral NPH
Extended drainage mandatory — single tap false-negative in complex cases
Counsel husband on realistic goals — gait improvement, not behavioral normalization
contraindicated_actions: Proceeding to VP shunt without extended drainage confirmation given single-tap borderline-negative
Attributing all behavioral and gait symptoms to bvFTD without NPH workup
Promising family that VP shunt will reverse behavioral disinhibition (bvFTD behavior will persist)
Genetic FTD testing without appropriate genetic counseling
key_reasoning_points: bvFTD can produce frontal release signs, behavioral disinhibition, and executive dysfunction that overlap with NPH features — FDG-PET is the key differentiator
Interval ventriculomegaly in a bvFTD patient signals superimposed NPH, not ex vacuo from FTD atrophy
Extended drainage confirmed NPH component (32%) missed by single tap (false-negative)
NfL 2840 pg/mL confirms aggressive neurodegeneration — sets expectations for limited cognitive/behavioral benefit of shunting
VP shunt is still appropriate for fall prevention and gait improvement — quality of life for caregivers

red_herrings.data_point: Prior diagnosis of bvFTD with frontal behavioral features and executive dysfunction
red_herrings.intended_effect: All symptoms attributed to bvFTD progression; NPH missed because behavioral disinhibition and executive dysfunction expected in FTD
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Interval ventriculomegaly and positive extended drainage reveal superimposed NPH. bvFTD is real but NPH is the new treatable process.

red_herrings.intended_effect: Negative tap trial declared, NPH excluded, family counseled there is no treatable component
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Extended drainage reveals 32% TUG improvement — single tap false-negative. NPH component confirmed and warrants VP shunt.

red_herrings.data_point: Upward gaze slowing on exam and borderline MPAR on MRI
red_herrings.intended_effect: PSP diagnosis entertained, resulting in therapeutic nihilism and deferral of VP shunt
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Full PSP criteria not met. FDG-PET pattern is bvFTD not PSP. NPH-bvFTD is more likely than PSP.

metadata.difficulty_variant_description: Diagnostic puzzle NPH — superimposed on bvFTD; behavioral disinhibition overlaps with FTD symptoms; single tap borderline-negative requiring extended drainage; FDG-PET and NfL essential; PSP as additional red herring.
